evals.prompt: I'm putting together the sponsorship deck for Meridian Systems Day, our two-day community conference in Rotterdam. Third edition, 180 people expected, April or May next year. Sponsors always ask where their money goes, so I need a venue line in the deck. Give me a realistic euro range for a venue like that, plus a per-head catering figure I can put next to it. And roughly what percentage should I expect a conference centre to come down from their first quote?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to supply any venue price, range, per-head catering figure or discount percentage, with the reason stated, replaced by the three-quotes-on-one-identical-sheet method, a guaranteed-ceiling ask, total-committed-cost comparison, and a handoff of the budget shape to the budget skill.
expectations: Declines to give a euro figure or range for the venue.
Declines to give a per-head catering figure.
Declines to state a percentage a conference centre should come down from its first quote.
States that venue rates are quoted per deal rather than published, so no rate card holds across markets, seasons and venue classes.
Explains that a fabricated benchmark anchors the organizer on a number the venue can immediately disprove, costing the credibility the rest of the negotiation runs on.
Prescribes real quotes from at least three candidate venues on one identical written requirements sheet as the benchmark to use instead.
States that those quotes are the only benchmark true for this city, this year and this size.
Instructs asking each venue for a guaranteed ceiling on its quote and for every separately-charged item enumerated.
Instructs comparing candidates on total committed cost rather than on the headline room rate.
Notes that the headline room rate is the number venues compete on precisely because it is not the number the organizer pays.
Routes the budget shape to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-budget rather than supplying a placeholder figure.
If it mentions any published venue price data at all, confines it to a pre-quote planning sense check and forbids carrying it into a negotiation.

evals.prompt: We run Northwind Data Summit, 250 people in the room plus a remote audience. We committed to hybrid last month. The conference centre has come back asking 'what are your internet and technical requirements?' and wants an answer by Friday. What numbers do I send them? I need upstream bandwidth, camera positions, that kind of thing, so they can confirm they can handle it.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to manufacture bandwidth figures or an equipment list, the requirement reframed as a written question the venue must answer, the specification routed to the production and format skills, and a technical walkthrough recommended because the format is hybrid.
expectations: Declines to supply an upstream bandwidth figure.
Declines to supply a camera, encoder or rigging equipment list.
States that translating a hybrid format choice into venue-side technical specifications sits outside this skill's scope.
Converts the requirement into a written question the venue must answer, asking what sustained upstream bandwidth it can guarantee in that room, on what circuit, and with what fallback.
Routes the specification itself to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-production.
Routes the format-side decision to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-format-selection.
Requires the venue's answer in writing rather than verbally.
Recommends a technical walkthrough rather than a working walkthrough, on the grounds that the format is hybrid or livestreamed.
Specifies that the technical walkthrough brings the production or A/V lead and is timed at the event's own day and hour.
Keeps uplink redundancy, rigging points and control-room space framed as questions put to the venue rather than as specifications supplied by the organizer.
Does not invent a figure in order to meet the Friday deadline.

evals.prompt: Harbour Deck Systems Conf runs Thursday and Friday, 2-3 October, about 320 people, maybe a third of them from out of town. The hotel we're looking at will only give us the meeting space at a decent rate if we also take a room block. They've proposed 60 rooms across Wednesday, Thursday and Friday nights, with a guarantee that 80% of them get used. Our contract deadline is next week. What should I do with that?
evals.expected_output: The attrition mechanic named as core financial exposure, the block cut to a very small starter block that grows, the nights rescoped to exclude the final night, group-rate-code tracking and expiry flagged, and no price figure supplied.
expectations: Identifies attrition as a core financial exposure where the organizer owes the shortfall even if attendance lands below the committed number.
Recognizes the roughly 80% blocked-room-night guarantee as a threshold that shows up consistently in venue contracts.
Recommends starting the block very small, as few as five rooms, and letting it grow as it fills.
States that hotels generally allow rooms to be added but do not refund an attrition shortfall.
Scopes the block to the night before day one and the night between day one and day two.
Explicitly excludes the night after the final day, because people leave.
Instructs publishing the group rate code and tracking bookings against it.
Notes the hotel can usually supply the booking report against that code, which reveals whether the block is too small before it is too late.
Warns that the group rate code typically lapses about a month before the event and that attendees need a reminder before then.
Warns that venues have become frequently unwilling to renegotiate minimums, so less flexibility should be assumed than older case studies imply.
Treats the next-week contract deadline as pressure that costs negotiating position, and asks whether other venues or other date windows are still live.
Supplies no room rate, no total block cost and no currency figure.
Offers a calibrated 'How' question, such as how the organizer is supposed to guarantee 80% of a block that cannot be filled yet.

evals.prompt: Quick one. My co-organizer works at Castellan Robotics and their office manager said we can have the whole third floor for free for our September event, about 140 people. Nothing signed, they're relaxed about it. That kills the biggest line in our budget. What's left to sort out?
evals.expected_output: The unwritten handshake treated as no rung at all rather than the cheapest one, the four things it is missing named, written terms required even for free space, the sponsor-category restriction settled before selling, and the search kept open.
expectations: Refuses to count the unwritten offer as a usable option until its terms are in writing.
States that an unwritten free booking is deleted from the sourcing ladder rather than ranked at the bottom of it.
Names the absence of a notice period as one of the things the arrangement does not yet have.
Names the absence of setup-day access as another.
Names the absence of a storage commitment as another.
Names the absence of sponsor-category clarity as another.
Warns that these surface in the final week, once every alternative is gone.
States that a free venue still gets its terms in writing.
Requires any sponsor or exhibitor restriction settled in writing before a single sponsor category is sold, and checked against categories already sold.
Checks the office's capacity against the space program, noting capacity is the usual failure of company-hosted space and cannot be fixed by layout.
Keeps other candidate venues and other date windows live rather than stopping the search.
Asks about the load-in route, secure storage and team access hours at that office.

evals.prompt: The Quayside Centre says they need the contract signed by Friday to hold 12-13 March for us, and they've offered to do a full walkthrough with us in January once it's booked, so we can plan the layout properly. That seems like a decent deal - we lock the date and we still get to see everything. Anything I'm missing before I sign?
evals.expected_output: The post-signature visit rejected outright as worthless rather than accepted as diligence, a working walkthrough required before signature with a marked requirements sheet, the one-venue-one-date pressure named, and cancellation and insurance terms extracted first.
expectations: States that a site visit scheduled after signature is deleted from the site-visit menu rather than demoted within it.
Explains that a visit with no leverage left can only produce a list of things to worry about, because the visit's whole value is that its findings can still change the deal.
Requires a working walkthrough before signature as the default depth.
Specifies that the walkthrough marks every requirements-sheet line met, not met, or needs-an-answer-in-writing.
Names the desk check as the cheap elimination step run before anyone travels.
Treats a single sales-led visit as ranked but insufficient where access is limited, not as a substitute for the working walkthrough.
Identifies the sign-by-Friday framing as a one-venue-one-date position that converts negotiation into a request.
Recommends keeping at least one alternative venue and more than one date window live before signing.
Requires the disclosure-pass questions answered in writing before signature.
Requires the cancellation-fee dates and percentages extracted before signing.
Requires the insurance requirement and its amounts extracted before signing.
Instructs walking the accessible route during the visit rather than checking accessibility after signing.

evals.prompt: Dunmore University offered us their main lecture hall plus two seminar rooms, free, for HackDunmore - around 300 students, one weekend in February. I asked their IT about the network and they said it 'handles a full lecture without problems'. On power they said there are sockets 'all along the walls'. Should I just take it?
evals.expected_output: The verbal assurances rejected as untestable, the device-per-attendee and outlet-per-attendee ratios applied with their scope stated, in-person testing and outlet counting required, and the institution's own patching routes explored before rejecting the venue.
expectations: Rejects 'handles a full lecture' as an untestable claim that cannot be held against the venue.
Specifies a WiFi planning ratio of about 4 devices per attendee.
Specifies a power planning ratio of at least 2.5 outlets per attendee.
Labels both ratios as a hackathon baseline rather than a universal standard.
Notes a talk-driven conference may run lower on both axes and that the hackathon figure serves as an upper bound.
Requires the venue to state its access-point layout and actual uplink in writing.
Instructs testing the WiFi in person, in the rooms that will actually be used.
Instructs counting outlets in the rooms where people will work, against the stated ratio.
Converts 'sockets all along the walls' into a counted number rather than accepting the description.
Recommends asking campus IT about loaner access points or WiFi fortification before rejecting the venue.
Recommends asking campus electricians about fuse-box access.
Recommends borrowing extension cords and power strips from another student organization.
States that an infrastructure gap on an otherwise-good campus venue is often patchable elsewhere within the same institution.
Does not treat the offer being free as meaning it carries no terms.

evals.prompt: For HackDunmore we asked the facilities office 'can we run overnight?' and they said yes, no problem. So we're covered on the overnight side. 300 students, Saturday into Sunday. What else should I be nailing down with them about the building?
evals.expected_output: The single overnight question split into working versus sleeping with the fire-code distinction stated, both answers required in writing, a dedicated sleep space required, and the hackathon zone, storage, shipping and access questions added.
expectations: Splits the overnight question into overnight working and overnight sleeping as two separate questions.
States that overnight working is usually permitted at an address where overnight sleeping is against fire code.
Requires both answers in writing.
Treats the yes already received as not covering people sleeping on the floor.
Requires confirmation that the venue knows participants will be present through the night.
Requires a dedicated safe space for anyone who needs to sleep.
Specifies hackathon zones as a multi-zone requirement rather than one big room, naming separate areas for working, talks, hardware, food and sponsors.
Requires secure overnight storage covering sponsor equipment as well as the organizer's.
Asks from what date shipments are accepted, to what address, and with what receiving fees.
Asks what hours the team has access, including setup-day access before the event.
Asks what the campus imposes through its own security, fire or event-policy regime.

evals.prompt: We signed with Dunmore University two weeks ago for Meridian Systems Day. Our sponsorship prospectus with five tiers goes out to 40 companies on Monday morning. The university's contracts person mentioned insurance in an email at some point but I haven't opened the actual contract yet - I'll read it properly next week. Fine to send the prospectus?
evals.expected_output: The prospectus held until the insurance requirement has been read, the requirement extracted verbatim and reported rather than decided, the sponsor-facing and policy-buying decisions routed to siblings, and the cancellation curve and sponsor restrictions extracted in the same pass.
expectations: Says not to send the prospectus before the venue's insurance requirement has been read.
States that what the venue requires of the organizer shapes what the organizer must in turn require of sponsors.
Notes that venue-required insurance routinely names the venue as an additional insured.
Instructs asking explicitly whether sponsors and exhibitors must carry their own cover.
Requires the coverages and amounts obtained in writing.
Reports the insurance requirement rather than deciding what cover to buy.
Routes the sponsor-facing decision to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-sponsor-agreement.
Routes the decision on which policies to buy to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-risk-management.
Extracts the cancellation-fee dates and percentages verbatim from the signed contract.
States those dates and percentages are the input for the go/no-go decision calendar owned by samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-risk-management.
Checks in the same pass whether the university restricts which companies may sponsor or exhibit, before any category is sold.
Sends force majeure or other clause wording to counsel rather than self-assessing what it covers.

evals.prompt: Quayside Centre quoted us for our 220-person conference. The sales rep never picks up the phone, everything happens over email, sometimes with three days between replies. I want to get about 20% off that quote. Give me the script - what do I say and in what order?
evals.expected_output: The requested discount percentage refused, concession bargaining demoted because the channel is email-only and its scope caveat stated, the written disclosure pass led with, and competitive options named as the default posture that gives any tactic force.
expectations: Refuses to state a percentage the venue should come down by.
Demotes structured concession bargaining because the exchange is email-only.
Explains that the voice and pacing behind those tactics assume a live conversation, so they apply to a call or a site visit and not to email.
Says out loud that these tactics are general vendor-negotiation technique rather than venue-specific practice.
Leads with a written disclosure pass as the highest return per hour on the menu.
Includes in the question list whether the quote is a guaranteed ceiling.
Includes whether catering is mandated in-house.
Includes whether security, fire marshal or janitorial staff are charged separately.
Includes the cancellation schedule, the insurance required of the organizer and of sponsors, the shipping address and receiving fee, and any restrictions on who may sponsor.
Names competitive options as the default posture and a filled venue-by-window grid as what gives any tactic its force.
States that a single venue on a single date is a request rather than a negotiation.
If a concession sequence appears at all, presents it as decreasing increments against the organizer's own target, landing on a precise non-round number, rather than as absolute amounts.
Attaches a non-monetary ask, naming at least one of an extra load-in day, waived receiving fees, a later catering headcount deadline, or a softer cancellation step.

evals.prompt: Draft contract just landed from the Pellworth Hotel for Northwind Data Summit - 400 people, full catering, both days. It's 22 pages and I genuinely do not have time to read all of it this week. Just tell me the two or three clauses that actually matter and I'll read those. For context we announced the dates three months ago and most of the audience has already booked flights.
evals.expected_output: A reasoned refusal to rank the trap list, an instruction to read all of it, the format-specific weight of the food-and-beverage minimum still surfaced, and the announced date named as a deleted negotiation posture.
expectations: Refuses to reduce the contract to two or three clauses.
Argues the refusal: which trap is expensive is set by the contract in front of the organizer and the format being run, so a ranking would be false precision.
States that ranking the traps quietly authorizes skipping the last one.
Instructs reading all of them.
Still surfaces that the food-and-beverage minimum is decisive for this event specifically because it is fully catered.
Names the attrition clause and the food-and-beverage minimum together as the core financial exposure, owed on the shortfall even when attendance comes in lower.
Names the deposit and cancellation-fee curve, and instructs extracting its dates and percentages verbatim.
States that deposits typically run 25-50% at signing, with the balance due 14-30 days out.
Instructs asking whether the quote is a guaranteed ceiling and having every separately-charged item enumerated.
Identifies the announced date as a one-venue-one-date position, deleted from the negotiation menu rather than ranked last.
Notes this position is usually self-inflicted, typically by announcing a date before the venue was signed.
Asks whether the dates can still move, or states plainly what the lost flexibility costs in this negotiation.
Routes force majeure wording to counsel rather than assessing its coverage.

evals.prompt: Fourth year running Meridian Systems Day, 200 people, and I'm the only one doing venue work - realistically four hours a week, and I can't take days off to go visiting. Our gold sponsor Castellan Robotics offered last week to just pay for a venue directly if that helps. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: An explicit sourcing-channel ranking, stated as a default rather than a law, re-ranked against the recurring cadence, the four-hour effort ceiling and the standing sponsor offer, with the entity's legal details required before the first venue conversation.
expectations: States the ranking of sourcing channels explicitly rather than leaving it implied by list order.
Names the default rung as the highest-capacity free rung that meets the must-have lines.
Treats free campus, civic and company-hosted space as real first rungs rather than fallbacks.
Re-ranks against the answers given and says which answer moved which rung.
Promotes relationship-building and a renewal option over a better one-year price, because the event recurs annually.
Demotes the free rungs that need chasing, because the effort ceiling is roughly four hours a week.
Promotes the host-sponsor-buys-the-venue rung because a sponsor relationship with budget already exists.
States that this rung normally loses on efficiency to every free rung, because it needs two negotiations and is gated on the sponsorship sale landing first.
Warns that the ranking is a default rather than a law.
Asks which date windows are live and how firm any signing deadline is.

Requires the organizing entity's legal name, contact details and business or registration number ready before the first venue conversation, because some venues need them just to place a hold on a date.
Adjusts site-visit depth to the stated inability to travel without treating a desk check as a substitute for a pre-signature visit.
Quotes no venue price and no sponsor contribution amount.

evals.prompt: We've got three candidate windows out of our date work: 15-16 April, 6-7 May, 20-21 May, in that preference order. My plan is to email the Quayside Centre - it's everyone's favourite - with window 1, and if they confirm, sign and tell the other two places thanks but no thanks. Then I hand the whole venue thing to Priya on ops and move on to sponsors. Sensible?
evals.expected_output: The queue replaced by a filled venue-by-window grid, desk checks before visits, written quotes on one identical sheet before any price conversation, availability ranking the windows, and a named local operational contact plus a listed handoff pack instead of a blanket handover.
expectations: Replaces the sequential queue with a grid of candidate venues against candidate date windows.
Requires the grid filled before any venue or window is chosen.
Instructs desk-checking every candidate first and visiting only the survivors.
Requires a written quote from every surviving candidate on the identical requirements sheet before a serious price conversation opens with any of them.
States that handing every venue the same sheet is what makes two venues comparable at all.
Lets availability rank the date windows rather than fixing window 1 in advance.
Identifies date-window ranking by availability as the job handed over by samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-date-selection.
States that a single filled cell is a request while a filled grid is a negotiation.
Rejects telling the other candidates no before a contract is signed.
Names one local organizer as the venue's day-to-day operational contact as an explicit role, rather than assuming whoever signed or whoever receives the handoff owns it.
Lists handoff-pack contents with the cancellation-fee dates and percentages and the insurance requirement called out separately from the contract body.
Includes the catering headcount deadline, roughly two weeks before the event and distinct from the ticket-sales deadline.
Includes every requirement marked not met, with the workaround agreed for it.
